subject: microbiology
title: Vibrio cholerae, Campylobacter and Helicobacter

steps.tx: **Vibrio cholerae O1 and O139** (comma shaped, darting motility, oxidase positive, halotolerant) colonise small bowel without invading, releasing **AB cholera toxin** that ADP ribosylates Gs, locking adenylate cyclase on so cAMP pours chloride and water into the lumen. The result is painless **rice water stools** (no blood, no pus, no fever, no tenesmus) with isotonic dehydration, hypokalaemic ileus and shock. O139 Bengal emerged with epidemic potential like O1; non O1 vibrios cause wound sepsis (V. vulnificus in cirrhotics, V. parahaemolyticus Kanagawa seafood).
steps.say: Painless rice water without blood is cholera toxin at work. O1 and O139 both epidemic.

vis.alt: Diagram showing Vibrio cholerae in small bowel, its AB toxin activating Gs protein, leading to increased cAMP, and efflux of chloride and water, causing rice water stools.
vis.caption: Cholera toxin mechanism causes massive fluid loss, leading to rice water stools

steps.tx: **Cholera management** is fluids first: **oral rehydration solution** (glucose sodium co transport) for most, **Ringer lactate** intravenously for shock with potassium watched, antibiotics only shortening shedding (**single dose doxycycline**, azithromycin in pregnancy). Diagnosis uses **TCBS agar** (yellow sucrose fermenting colonies), dark field darting motility inhibited by antiserum, and Cary-Blair transport. **Shanchol killed oral vaccine** protects endemic belts; sanitation ends epidemics. Tetracycline shortens but never replaces volume.
steps.say: Cholera kills by volume loss: replace volume first. TCBS yellows the diagnosis.

steps.tx: **Campylobacter jejuni** (curved gull wing rods, microaerophilic, growth at 42C selecting poultry isolates) causes bloody inflammatory diarrhoea with cramps and fever, and its lipooligosaccharide mimics **GM1 ganglioside** triggering **Guillain-Barre syndrome** weeks later (ascending paralysis needing IVIG or plasmapheresis). Diagnosis is stool culture on Skirrow agar with oxidase; treatment is **azithromycin** (erythromycin) as fluoroquinolone resistance spreads. Reactive arthritis (HLA-B27) follows like Salmonella and Shigella.
steps.say: Bloody poultry diarrhoea then ascending paralysis is Campylobacter to Guillain-Barre. Azithromycin treats.

steps.tx: **Helicobacter pylori** (curved, **urease** splitting urea into ammonia cloud, antral coloniser) causes chronic gastritis, **duodenal ulcers**, gastric adenocarcinoma and **MALT lymphoma** (curable by eradication). Noninvasive diagnosis is **urea breath test or stool antigen**; invasive is rapid urease (CLO) on biopsy with histology. Eradication is **clarithromycin triple** (PPI plus amoxicillin plus clarithromycin) or **bismuth quadruple** where resistance rules; **test of cure** uses breath or stool antigen (never serology, antibodies linger). NSAID ulcers differ by history.
steps.say: Urease positive antral gastritis with ulcer is H. pylori. Cure MALT by eradication; retest with breath, not blood.
